stories.title: GWonMac 2026.11.0
stories.summary: A new launcher for all your accounts, the Hub search in every game window, Switch Character, map guidance, and a built-in Guide. Your accounts, builds, and settings come with you.
stories.body:
A new launcher for all your accounts, the Hub search in every game window, Switch Character, map guidance, and a built-in Guide. Your accounts, builds, and settings come with you.

- **A launcher for every account:** The launcher opens first. Choose **Play** for one account, or select several and open them together. **Accounts → Add account** creates another account with its own game window and sign-in. Your existing account is now **Main account**, with its login, builds, templates, and game files unchanged.
- **Hub:** Press <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>R</kbd> in a game window to search characters, accounts, travel destinations, builds, people, maps, and settings in one place. It works even with Tools off.
- **Switch Character:** Press <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> to change character from an outpost or the character screen.
- **Maps:** With Tools on, the :setting[Maps]{to="maps"} tool shows unexplored areas, walkable terrain, compass ranges, and an elite skill planner on the World Map.
- **More Tools:** Whispers (<kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd>), Travel to friends and your Guild Hall, Quick Item Move, Effect Timers, Reminders, an Alcohol Timer, and Chat Filters. Each one is optional; turn them on in :setting[Tools]{to="tools"}.
- **Texture packs:** Import TexMod `.tpf` packs in :setting[Texture packs]{to="texture-packs"}.
- **Home and Help:** Home shows news and today's Zaishen, Shining Blade, Vanguard, and Nicholas Sandford rotations. Help has a Guide, the open issues in ArenaNet's client with what you can do, and a way to send us a message.

## What works differently now

- <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>R</kbd> opens the Hub. To reload a game window, press <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>Q</kbd> and choose **Reload Guild Wars**.
- Xunlai Storage opens with <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd>. Shortcuts you changed yourself stay as they are.
- Settings is one page with sections for Tools, Maps, Appearance, Game, Texture packs, Game files, Updates, Home screen, and Advanced. Open it with <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>,</kbd> or the gear in the launcher.
- Build templates are now in the [Build Library]($docs/guides/templates). **Template files** there imports and exports Windows `.txt` templates.

[Technical release record](https://github.com/Mat4m0/gwonmac/releases/tag/v2026.11.0){target="_blank"}

stories.title: GWonMac 2026.8.10
stories.summary: Adds Kamadan trade chat, Fast Reload, and smarter Quick Travel, plus skill key labels and cooldown timers. Tools features are now built to survive small Guild Wars updates.
stories.body:
Adds Kamadan trade chat, Fast Reload, and smarter Quick Travel, plus skill key labels and cooldown timers. Tools features are now built to survive small Guild Wars updates.

- **Kamadan Trade Chat (`⌘K`):** browse trade messages and check merchant and trader prices in the game.
- **Fast Reload (`⌘Q`):** restarts only your current Guild Wars session in a few seconds. Select **Return to my character automatically** to log back in to the same character. Use it when memory or texture problems appear.
- **Quick Travel (`⌘T`):** shows only destinations your account can reach, keeps recent destinations per character, and supports `Tab` to move between results.
- **Settings → Display:** choose between two interface styles, or create and apply your own theme.
- **Settings → Display → Controller button symbols:** PlayStation symbols, from the next game start.
- **Settings → Tools → Skill key labels:** custom shortcuts such as `Shift+C` show over the correct skill slot.
- **Settings → Tools → Skill cooldown timers:** remaining recharge time shows over your skills.
- **Input:** many keyboard shortcuts (`⌘K`, `⌘C`, `⌘V`) and mouse actions behave more consistently, and movement keys no longer stick.
- **Windows:** the game window keeps its place when you connect or remove a display.
- **Diagnostics:** clearer reports for Tools, reload failures, and graphics or texture problems.

## Known issues

- The Guild Wars memory limit is not fixed. Fast Reload is the quickest way to recover; the Reload action in the memory warning uses it too.

[Technical release record](https://github.com/Mat4m0/gwonmac/releases/tag/v2026.8.10){target="_blank"}

stories.title: GWonMac 2026.8.9
stories.summary: Click and double-click work as before again, Tools is restored, and small routine Guild Wars updates should no longer break GWonMac.
stories.body:
Click and double-click work as before again, Tools is restored, and small routine Guild Wars updates should no longer break GWonMac.

- **Mouse:** click and double-click behave as in the original game again.
- **Tools:** all GWonMac Tools work again.
- **Quick Travel:** lists every location, remembers your recent destinations, and lets you add your own.
- **Xunlai Chest:** opens only when your account has access to it.
- **Keyboard:** modifier keys, macOS text-editing shortcuts, and held keys in chat now behave as expected, and movement no longer continues after you release `⌘`.
- **Multiple Accounts:** accounts in the background keep running.
- **Future updates:** small routine Guild Wars updates should no longer affect your game or need an emergency GWonMac update. A larger update can still break something.

[Technical release record](https://github.com/Mat4m0/gwonmac/releases/tag/v2026.8.9){target="_blank"}

stories.title: GWonMac 2026.8.8
stories.summary: Multiple Accounts arrives, Build Management is fully back, and Quick Travel and the Xunlai Chest open with a shortcut. All new gameplay features are opt-in and unavailable in PvP.
stories.body:
Multiple Accounts arrives, Build Management is fully back, and Quick Travel and the Xunlai Chest open with a shortcut. All new gameplay features are opt-in and unavailable in PvP.

- **Multiple Accounts:** run several Guild Wars sessions at the same time, each with its own sign-in.
- **Hero and Build Management (`⌘B`):** fully restored.
- **Quick Travel:** type `/tp` or press `⌘T` to travel to a location.
- **Xunlai Chest:** type `/chest` or press `⌘⇧C` in an outpost to open your storage.
- **Settings:** you can change every Tools shortcut if the defaults do not suit you.
- **Font:** every GWonMac interface now uses the original Guild Wars typeface.
- **Audio:** game sound keeps playing while you use GWonMac controls.
- **Keyboard:** the sign-in screen and in-game overlays now take keyboard input reliably.

## Notes

- If you do not enable Tools, its feature code does not run at all, and nothing changes for you.
- Like Toolbox, Tools is unavailable in PvP areas.
- Larger Toolbox features are not planned. If you cannot play without one, Windows or a Windows virtual machine is probably the better option.

[Technical release record](https://github.com/Mat4m0/gwonmac/releases/tag/v2026.8.8){target="_blank"}

stories.title: GWonMac Tools Beta is here
stories.summary: Release 2026.8.5 adds local build and team management, template import and export, an experimental 4 GB memory limit, and two interface styles.
stories.body:
Release `2026.8.5` introduces **GWonMac Tools Beta**: a local build and team manager made specifically for Guild Wars on Mac.

You can capture your current party, create player and hero builds, reorder heroes and skills, share complete teams, and apply a saved setup from a supported PvE outpost. The release also adds template import and export, an experimental 4 GB memory limit, and two interface styles.

![A saved player-and-hero team open in GWonMac Tools](/blog/2026-8-5/tools.jpeg)

GWToolbox++ itself still cannot run because it depends on the Windows client. GWonMac Tools is not a Toolbox replacement, but it brings some of its most-requested quality-of-life features to Mac players.

## A local home for builds and teams

GWonMac Tools adds a build library designed around the way people actually prepare a Guild Wars party.

You can:

- Save and edit player and hero builds
- Capture your current party as a reusable team
- Keep related variants without duplicating everything by hand
- Edit professions, attributes, skill bars, and hero behavior
- Reorder heroes and skills with drag and drop or the keyboard
- Search skills and browse them in attribute groups
- Filter for skills that fit the active slot or are currently unlocked
- Delete builds and teams with confirmation and Undo

Individual builds can be shared with standard Guild Wars template codes. Complete teams can be imported and exported with a GWonMac team code, keeping the player, heroes, builds, attributes, behavior, difficulty, and notes together.

## Apply a saved team

From a supported PvE outpost, **Apply team** can configure:

- Normal or Hard Mode
- The player's build
- Hero roster and order
- Player and hero professions
- Skill bars and attributes
- Hero behavior

Team Management is a **Beta** feature. Hard Mode support is included, but additional live tester coverage is welcome.

## Templates work without Tools

Build-template migration is a Core feature and does not require enabling GWonMac Tools.

Under **Settings → Templates**, you can:

- Import an old Windows Guild Wars template folder
- Import templates from files
- Import one or many template codes from the clipboard
- Export your templates
- Recover templates stored in unexpected subfolders

Sign in to Guild Wars before opening the Templates pane. If you opened Templates
while the game was still starting, reopen the pane after signing in so the
controls can connect to the game's storage.

You can also publish a build from Tools into Guild Wars. The Tools library and the game's Templates folder remain separate, so editing one never unexpectedly rewrites the other.

Read the [template migration guide](/docs/guides/templates) for the complete workflow.

## More memory headroom for long sessions

Guild Wars normally has a 2 GB memory limit. Very long sessions can eventually approach it and may need a reload.

You can now opt into an experimental 4 GB limit under:

**Settings → Advanced → Experimental 4 GB memory limit**

The option is off by default and requires restarting Guild Wars. Settings shows whether the current session is using 2 GB or 4 GB.

The larger limit provides more headroom and may help during long sessions. It does **not** stop memory from continuing to grow. If 4 GB mode is unavailable for the current Guild Wars version, GWonMac safely starts in normal 2 GB mode instead.

The new memory warning stays out of the way and lets you reload Guild Wars directly when the current session is running low.

## Choose your interface

The in-game interface has been redesigned with two styles:

- **Guild Wars** remains the default and closely follows the original game's ornamental interface.
- **Obsidian** offers a quieter, borderless charcoal design with restrained gold accents.

Choose between them under:

**Settings → Display → Interface style**

Both styles provide the same features, responsive layouts, profession colors, and adjustable panel visibility.

![The Guild Wars interface style in GWonMac Settings](/blog/2026-8-5/ui_guild-wars.png)

![The borderless Obsidian interface style in GWonMac Settings](/blog/2026-8-5/ui_obsidian.png)

## What Beta means

GWonMac Tools is optional and off by default. Enable it under:

**Settings → Controls → GWonMac Tools Beta**

![Enable GWonMac Tools Beta under Settings and Controls](/blog/2026-8-5/enable_tools.png)

The first enable requires restarting Guild Wars. After that restart, individual tool settings can be changed while the game is running.

Tools is unavailable in PvP, guild halls, and unsupported regions. Core features such as the native cursor and template import/export continue to work independently.

After a Guild Wars update, Tools may be temporarily unavailable until a compatible GWonMac update is ready. You can always continue playing normally.

Builds, teams, and preferences stay on this Mac. GWonMac does not upload your library, account, or gameplay data.

## Help test the release

The most useful feedback now is:

- Repeated Team Apply runs with different hero professions and skill bars
- Normal and Hard Mode application
- Larger or unusual hero rosters
- Long sessions using the experimental 4 GB limit
- Interface and layout behavior on smaller Mac displays

If something fails, tell us what you expected, what Guild Wars showed afterward, and which Mac you use.
